reason: The cited evidence demonstrates ODS strengthening in a different HEA system (Al0.3CoCrFeMnNi) at lower temperature (800 °C) and with a different matrix structure, but provides no data on refractory BCC HEAs, Y2O3 stability at 1273 K, or the specific TiVNbTa alloy. The key premises about dispersion feasibility, thermal stability, and strength gains in this specific system are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a refractory BCC HEA via powder metallurgy
Y2O3 dispersoids remain thermally stable and pin dislocations at 1273 K in a TiVNbTa matrix
ODS strengthening magnitude observed in CoCrFeMnNi HEA (400 to 800 MPa at 800 °C) translates to similar gains in TiVNbTa at 1273 K
